content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain cooked noodles are a ready‑to‑eat product made from whole wheat grains that have been steamed or boiled. They retain most of the fiber, vitamins, and minerals found in the intact grain and have a soft texture suitable for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain noodles contain more dietary fiber than refined‑flour noodles.
They are a staple in many Asian cuisines, used in soups, salads, and stir‑fries.
Cooked whole‑grain noodles have a lower glycemic index compared with white pasta.
Production involves minimal grain processing, preserving more nutrients.
They can be made from various whole grains such as wheat, spelt, or rye.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2, and B3 aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Provides iron, magnesium, and zinc, essential for blood formation, muscle function, and immunity.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps maintain stable glucose levels, beneficial for individuals with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Plant protein and healthy fats contribute to cardiovascular wellbeing.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Made from wheat, it contains gluten and may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some pre‑flavored versions can be high in salt; check the label if you need to limit sodium.

items.title: Moisture absorption
items.content: Improper storage can cause the noodles to absorb moisture, become soggy, or develop mold.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the noodles to hot soups, toss them cold in salads with vegetables and soy sauce, or quickly stir‑fry with veggies and protein. Typically, a brief 2–3 minute boil in hot water is enough to reheat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a dry, cool place in a sealed package. After opening, use within 1–2 weeks or refrigerate if you won’t consume them quickly.
